name: Matrixyl 3000
lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex made by Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, and is used in anti-wrinkle serums. [3] Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), was launched by Sederma in 2000. [4]

Published evidence on the blend itself is limited: a 2026 permeation study reported that both peptides were detected in layers of the stratum corneum of three volunteers but appeared to remain between cells. [3]

paras: The two peptides are lipid-modified fragments proposed to signal skin cells about matrix repair and inflammation. A patent application lists oligopeptide derivatives with acyl groups combined with apple extract for wrinkles, tested in 42 women aged 40 to 70 around the eyes over four weeks. [1]

No independent trial of Matrixyl 3000 itself was found. The permeation study above examined its two peptides in serums on three volunteers. [3] Wikipedia states that efficacy statements on the original Matrixyl are tagged as needing medical citation. [4]

quick.overview:
Matrixyl 3000 is a branded pairing of two lab-made peptides used in anti-wrinkle serums.

Independent published human data on the blend are limited.
quick.mechanism: Its peptides are proposed to signal skin cells to repair matrix and reduce inflammation; one study found they stay in the skin surface layers.
quick.risks: A cosmetic ingredient; no blend-specific safety data were found in the sources reviewed.
